text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- ABN AMRO board menber resigns as a result of
wife's insider trading. (p1)
- Trading company Hagemeyer books 14 pct higher 1996 net, forecasts further profits growth. (p1)
- European Commission to send veterinary inspectors to Netherlands to check on irregularities in pig exports to Italy. (p1)
- Rabobank sees further earnings growth; the bank revealed bad debt provisions of Dfl 3.45 billion. (p1)
- Food ingredients boost Gist -Brocades net by 10 percent. (p3)
- Fresh speculation about possible alliances between Spain's Iberia and KLM. (p3)
- Talks about bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker's re-launch chill off. (p3)
- Accountant Deloitte & Touche to form alliance with lawyers and notaries firm Van Anken Knueppe Damstra. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm puts up Dfl 2 billion to make good shortfall in social funds. (p1)
- Telfort, the telecoms firm of Dutch rail (NS) and British Telecom, demands Economics Affairs Minister Hans Wijers intervene in conflict with PTT Telecom. (p2)
- State misses out on billions of guilders in tax and premiums because of strong mortgage growth. (p3)
- Cabinet wants to stick to growth limits it set in 1995 for Schiphol airport. (p7)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Some 15 prominent Dutchmen set up Republican Society to re-open discussion on Dutch state post-Queen Beatrix. (p1)
- KLM tickets are up to Dfl 1,100 cheaper in Belgium, Germany and England. (p9)
- Justice ministry has little success in prosecuting insider trading cases. (p33)
- Insurer Delta Lloyd's 1996 net pressured by European single currency provisions. (p35)
TROUW
- Cabinet targets second airport in the sea to enable further growth in air traffic. (p1)
- Many Rabobank clients sold their shares late last year, fearing correction. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Electronics firm Neways 1996 net rises five percent to Dfl 6.3 million. (p11)
- German shipbuilder Jos Meyer seeks expansion in Eemshaven in province of Groningen. (p12)
